{{Short description|2009 book by Kevin Houston}}
{{italic title}}
'''''How to Think Like a Mathematician: A Companion to Undergraduate Mathematics''''' is a book by Kevin Houston, a [[senior lecturer]] in mathematics at the [[University of Leeds]]. It was published in 2009 by [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Houston |first1=Kevin |title=How to Think Like a Mathematician: A Companion to Undergraduate Mathematics |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/how-to-think-like-a-mathematician/FB0813C3AEDDECD40BE58AF186370D52 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |access-date=2 January 2024 |date=2009|doi=10.1017/CBO9780511808258 |isbn=978-0-521-89546-0 }}</ref>

The book targets current and incoming [[undergraduate education|undergraduate]] students of mathematics, and focuses on the [[Language of mathematics|
mathematical language]] and techniques required for [[mathematical proof|proof]] writing.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Leversha |first1=Gerry |title=Review of How to think like a mathematician |journal=The Mathematical Gazette |date=July 2010 |volume=94 |issue=530 |pages=369–371 |doi=10.1017/S0025557200006938 |jstor=25759706 |s2cid=183890441 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25759706 |access-date=2 January 2024 |issn=0025-5572}}</ref><ref name="IntermontMAA">{{cite web |last1=Intermont |first1=Michele |date=4 July 2009 |title=How to Think Like a Mathematician: A Companion to Undergraduate Mathematics |url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/how-to-think-like-a-mathematician-a-companion-to-undergraduate-mathematics |access-date=2 January 2024 |website=[[Mathematical Association of America]] |publisher=}}</ref>

== Summary ==
The book is divided into five chapters:
# ''Study skills for mathematicians''
# ''How to think logically''
# ''Definitions, theorems and proofs''
# ''Techniques of proof''
# ''Mathematics that all mathematicians need''

== Reception ==
Michele Intermont of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] described the book as a "wonderful resource".<ref name="IntermontMAA" /> {{ill|Franz Lemmermeyer|de}} remarked that "the book is clearly written and contains suggestions and exercises from which not only undergraduates, but also highschool students can benefit".<ref>Franz Lemmermeyer, ''zbMATH'', {{zbl|1158.00001}}</ref>
